RG-007.01.duty: The flow names a distinct Inner layer and Outer layer.
The two selected tunnels have independent key contexts.

RG-007.02.duty: Each tunnel joins infrastructure devices at different sites and at its own layer.
An IPsec tunnel terminates on VPN gateways.
A MACsec tunnel terminates on MACsec devices.
RG-007.02.condition: All four encrypted layers use IPsec.

RG-007.02.duty: The Inner endpoints belong to the declared Red networks. The corresponding Outer endpoints are at the same respective sites.

RG-007.04.duty: Every certificate-authenticated component has a responsible certificate authority.
A component that uses a pre-shared connectivity-association key has a key generator.
RG-007.04.condition: The IPsec deployments use certificate authentication.

RG-007.04.duty: Different-level Inners sharing an Outer require a Gray Firewall.
RG-007.04.condition: These two profiles share an Outer across multiple levels.

RG-007.05.duty: The flow selected at injection starts on the actual Red network.
Gray egress has exactly the selected Inner layer and an earlier matching encryption event.

RG-007.06.duty: Black egress carries the selected Outer layer around the selected Inner layer.
Inner encryption occurred before Outer encryption and both preceded Black egress.
Protected traffic received on Black carries both selected layers in that order.

RG-007.07.duty: After crossing Black, plaintext delivery reaches the destination of the injected flow.
Outer decryption preceded Inner decryption and both preceded delivery.

RG-008.01.duty: The declared Red networks have dedicated Inner assignments.
Each assigned device is an Inner at its Red network’s full security level.

RG-008.02.duty: Both endpoints of each authenticated pair and each established Inner tunnel are Inner devices.
Authenticated Inner peers have the same full security label.
RG-008.02.condition: A cross-level fault requires two different labels.

RG-008.02.duty: Established Inner tunnel endpoints have the same full security label.
RG-008.02.condition: A cross-level fault requires two different labels.

RG-008.04.duty: Each declared cross-site peer pair has a realizable path from injection to plaintext delivery.

RG-008.06.duty: An included Unclassified Red network has its own Inner.
All applicable Red duties also apply to the included Unclassified network. Physical separation has an independently documented pre-existing failure on both applicable profiles.

RG-013.01.duty: Every Gray path between different-level Inners visits a Gray Firewall.
A Gray Firewall exists whenever there are Inners at two different levels.

RG-013.02.duty: A Gray administrative workstation is at the highest applicable level.
A locally run Gray CA is placed at the highest level.
RG-013.02.condition: The certificate authorities in these profiles are worker-hosted.

RG-013.02.duty: The specified management-to-Inner paths visit a Gray Firewall. Admitted traffic between the identified manager and a lower-level Inner is blocked in both directions.
The same path restriction applies to a Gray revocation service.
RG-013.02.condition: The four profiles distribute files for revocation checking.

RG-013.03.duty: The Outer filters traffic between identified Inner peers by level and intended communication.
A Gray Firewall filters the identified Inner peers by the same conditions.

RG-013.04.duty: A Gray Firewall filters the relevant traffic.
The device receives the required physical protection.
Each Gray Firewall has a path from at least one Inner gateway.
Each Gray Firewall has a path to at least one Outer gateway.

RG-029.01.duty: The loaded Inner IPsec connection specifies ESP tunnel mode.
The Inner has an associated IP tunnel.

RG-029.02.duty: A non-control packet crossing from the internal side receives matching Inner encryption before external transmission.
A non-control external transmission contains the sender’s Inner layer and has an earlier encryption event.

RG-029.04.duty: The outbound mandatory-access-control policy is present when selected.
The inbound mandatory-access-control policy is present when selected.

RG-030.01.duty: The loaded Outer IPsec connection specifies ESP tunnel mode.
The Outer has an associated IP tunnel.
RG-030.01.condition: OR-1 explicitly calls for ESP tunnel mode. The Lean condition also records its associated IP tunnel.

RG-030.02.duty: A non-control packet crossing from the internal side receives matching Outer encryption before external transmission.
A non-control external transmission contains the sender’s Outer layer and has an earlier encryption event.

RG-030.04.duty: The outbound mandatory-access-control policy is present when selected.
The inbound mandatory-access-control policy is present when selected.

RG-034.02.duty: Each Outer attaches to the inside of an Outer Firewall.
That same firewall attaches to Black on its outside.

RG-034.04.duty: Each Outer reaches a Gray Firewall on its Gray side when one is required.
Each Outer reaches an Inner when a Gray Firewall is optional.
RG-034.04.condition: Net-02 has a single security level.

RG-035.01.duty: The Outer VPN’s Black-side rules admit only IPsec or approved control traffic in either direction.
An Outer MACsec device admits MACsec or approved control.
RG-035.01.condition: The four Outers are VPN gateways.

RG-035.01.duty: An outbound packet names an intended peer.

RG-035.02.duty: Inner Gray interfaces allow the designated tunnel protocols.
The separate control-traffic permission has both policy and authorizing-official approval.

RG-035.04.duty: The Outer Firewall admits only tunnel traffic or approved control.
On the inside, inbound non-control traffic identifies the local Outer as its source.
On the outside, inbound non-control traffic identifies the local Outer as its destination.

RG-038.01.duty: External multicast is rejected by the Outer.
The narrow exception concerns necessary, approved link control for an Outer MACsec peer.

RG-038.03.duty: An IPv4 VPN gateway accepts only TCP, UDP, ESP or ICMP.

RG-039.01.duty: A Gray workstation may originate the designated management traffic.
RG-039.01.condition: Only net-05 has Gray administrative workstations.

RG-039.01.duty: An Outer’s own management initiation is restricted to logging and authentication.

RG-039.02.duty: An appropriate same-level Inner tunnel exchange qualifies under the tunnel allowance.
The appropriate Gray management exchange qualifies when that service is present.
RG-039.02.condition: The original tunnel selectors cover the Red or Gray data networks. Even net-05 uses local management interfaces and declares no Gray management tunnel.

RG-039.02.duty: When an eligible carrier is used, the policy must identify its embedded Inner pair.
RG-039.02.condition: All four forwarding captures have an empty carrier inventory.

RG-039.03.duty: Approved protected data uses the designated same-level pair.
Alternatively, the data belongs to an appropriate Gray management tunnel.
RG-039.03.condition: The original tunnel selectors cover the Red or Gray data networks. Even net-05 uses local management interfaces and declares no Gray management tunnel.

RG-039.06.duty: Standalone approved control and management traffic satisfy the Outer policy.
Traffic with an independent tunnel allowance can qualify under that allowance.

RG-039.07.duty: Everything the local hook admits meets the restrictions and an allowance.
Every eligible packet satisfying both passes the local hook.

RG-040.03.duty: Necessary HTTP to a designated Inner revocation service is admitted.
RG-040.03.condition: None of the four profiles defines that service as a Gray data-plane endpoint.

RG-040.03.duty: Other HTTP is rejected when a Gray Firewall is required.

RG-040.04.duty: Admitted management traffic uses a physical interface connected to the Gray management network.
The management service is recognized and approved.

RG-040.07.duty: Traffic outside the allowed classes is denied.
An eligible permitted exchange passes the required local hook.
